title: Staged Migration & Safeguards — Rollout Tuning Notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working notes doc for a new console flow that supports staged model migrations (multi-step) with explicit safeguards and composable fallback policies. Goal is to capture UX decisions, wireframe sketches, tuning knobs, and a prioritized backlog of follow-ups. Focus: make migrations predictable and safe for product teams moving traffic between models/variants across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.

High-level requirements:
- Support arbitrary N-step staged migrations (eg. 3-step: 5% -> 25% -> 70% -> 100%).
- Allow time-window and metric-based progression (time, latency p95, error rate, quality eval pass rates).
- Provide explicit rollback triggers and soft/hard stop behaviors.
- Policy composability: fallback can be a single variant, a tiered fallback, or region-only routing.
- Expose simulation and dry-run UX before applying traffic changes.
- Clear surface of cost implications per step (approx % change in token cost).

Key personas:
- ML/platform engineer running model rollouts for a product feature.
- Product manager monitoring quality deltas and approving step progression.
- On-call SRE who needs fast rollback and incident context.

UX flow (sketch, step-by-step):
1) Create migration plan (New -> Staged migration): choose source model + target model(s). Optionally include a fallback set.
2) Define steps: for each step choose target traffic percent, min duration, progression condition(s). Default quick option: 6/24/72h with safe thresholds.
3) Advanced: add health constraints (latency p95 < X ms, error rate < Y%, recent eval score delta < Z), add custom webhook check (customer-specific).
4) Visual timeline: show steps as horizontally stacked segments with expected start/end times, expected traffic, and color-coded risk (green/yellow/red).
5) Pre-check & dry-run: simulator uses sampled historical traffic to estimate batching impact, latency shift, and estimated cost delta. Show likely token savings/cost increase.
6) Launch: plan moves to active. Each step shows live metrics and a 2-button control: (Pause) (Promote). Auto-promote if conditions met; auto-rollback if hard-threshold violated.

Wireframe notes (textual):
- Header: plan name, owner, status pill (draft | active | paused | completed | rolled-back).
- Timeline view (center): step bars with percentages annotated. Hover reveals constraints. Click step opens side panel for editing.
- Right rail: live health summary (latency p50/p95, errors, user-facing quality checks, token rate, cost estimate).
- Bottom: action bar with Promote / Pause / Rollback / Edit. Rollback opens quick rollback dialog that suggests a safe target (previous step or pinned fallback).

Policy DSL (UX representation):
- We should avoid exposing full DSL initially. Provide rule builder with presets: Time-based, Metric-based, Manual, Hybrid.
- Example preset UI: Metric-based -> select metric dropdown -> threshold operator -> window length.
- Allow attaching a simple templated webhook that returns pass/fail for customer-specific checks.

Safeguard patterns & edge cases:
- Dependency-aware health: if rollout touches models used by downstream services, surface a dependency map and require two approvals.
- Partial-region migrations: allow region-level overrides (eg route EU traffic to variant-B while US stays on A).
- Dual-write / shadowing: support an option to shadow requests to target model for quality eval without affecting user responses. Shadow mode should not count towards billing by default (opt-in).
- Batching/latency interactions: include a note explaining that small traffic percentages can have non-linear latency/cost effects due to batching thresholds. Simulator should warn on <3% traffic steps.

Observability & operator UX:
- Per-step trace link to SLO/trace view.
- Automatic incident snapshot if rollback triggered: include recent logs, failing request examples, cost spike table.
- Explainable rollback reason: UI should show which condition triggered auto-rollback (metric, webhook, region capacity) plus a suggested follow-up (increase capacity, revert quantization).

Backlog (priority ordered):
1) Simulator: create 1-click dry-run using 7-day traffic sample (PLATFORM-842).
2) Timeline edit-in-place (drag to change durations and percents).
3) Region override UI + map visualization.
4) Shadowing option + cost flag (billing toggle).
5) Dependency graph generation (auto-scan service catalogs).
6) Preset templates for common patterns (e.g., "rapid canary", "enterprise slow roll", "safety-first with approval").
7) Safeguard explanations microcopy and onboarding checklist for first migration.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How prescriptive should the console be about recommended step sizes? (Default: pragmatic presets; keep edit freedom).
- Should simulator estimate customer-visible quality delta? We can show model eval metric deltas if customer provides a quick eval set, but that's extra infra.
- Billing transparency vs noise: show cost delta prominently or hide behind an "estimate" toggle? Ops requested prominent cost nudges.
- Locking UX for private deployments: customers may require that plan changes go through their SSO approval flow — need an API hook.

Acceptance criteria for MVP:
- Users can create a 3-step staged migration and launch it to Hosted and Dedicated endpoints.
- Auto-promote when conditions met and show clear progression logs.
- Auto-rollback on hard thresholds with an incident snapshot.
- Dry-run simulation available and linked from the create flow.
- Minimal documentation + inline help tooltips.

Mock copy snippets (for UI):
- Plan name input placeholder: "e.g. migrate-search-model-v2-staged"
- Step label: "Step 2 — 25% traffic for 24h (auto-promote if p95 < 250ms and error_rate < 0.5%)"
- Rollback toast: "Rolled back to Step 1 due to error rate breach (1.2% > 0.5%) — view incident"
- Simulator warning: "Warning: estimated latency increase likely due to batching at low traffic slices"

Short notes for handoff to design & infra:
- Design: provide final timeline glyphs + hover states, mobile collapse behavior, and clear affordances for rollback. Emphasize primary actions (Promote, Pause, Rollback) and make rollback a 2-step flow.
- Infra: need traffic splitter hooks that support sub-percent routing accuracy, safe QA environment for simulator queries, and webhook evaluator service for custom checks.
- Telemetry: ensure we have step-level metrics and event log stream for audit + onboarding analytics.

Immediate next steps:
- Sync with infra owners (Ethan) on simulator feasibility and sampling policy (this week).
- Design spike: 2 quick wireframes for timeline + side-panel (Priya).
- Draft short runbook for auto-rollback handling for SREs (Lucas).

Notes-to-self:
- Keep UI language simple; avoid "canary" overload — users may not know the term. Use "staged migration" or "step rollout" in copy.
- Consider a default "safety budget" that reserves small percentage of traffic as a hot fallback pool.

References and inspiration:
- Internal: rollout patterns doc (internal link above), lessons from previous large model migration (ticket: INFRA-602).
- Extern: rollout experiences from feature flagging tools (e.g. LaunchDarkly flows) for timeline UX.

Status: rough draft, needs infra feasibility confirmation before design polishing.
